tasks.whyItMatters: Amazon SQS queues are regional resources. Keeping all work in eu-west-2 ensures that the queue URLs, Console view, and CLI commands refer to the same Region.

tasks.goal: Send one harmless message, poll for it, inspect the visible message details, and explicitly delete it.
tasks.title: 3. Send, Receive, Inspect, and Delete a Standard-Queue Message

cliSteps.command: aws sqs send-message --queue-url <standard-queue-url-from-task-2> --message-body "SQS basic test message" --region eu-west-2

tasks.whyItMatters: Receiving a message does not delete it. A consumer must explicitly delete a successfully processed message using its receipt handle.

tasks.goal: Set safe test values for queue retention, delivery delay, maximum message size, and long polling, then send one delayed test message.
tasks.title: 4. Configure a Delayed Message and Long Polling
tasks.feature: Amazon SQS queue parameters and delayed messages

cliSteps.warning: Attribute changes can take time to propagate. This command changes only sqs-basic-test-standard when the correct URL is supplied.

commands.explanation: Sets one-day retention, no queue-level delay, a 1 MiB maximum message size, and a 20-second queue-level receive wait time. Replace the placeholder with the Task 2 queue URL.

cliSteps.explanation: Sets one-day retention, no queue-level delay, a 1 MiB maximum message size, and a 20-second queue-level receive wait time. Replace the placeholder with the Task 2 queue URL.

cliSteps.command: aws sqs send-message --queue-url <standard-queue-url-from-task-2> --message-body "Delayed SQS test message" --delay-seconds 10 --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.warning: Per-message delay is supported for standard queues and is limited to 900 seconds.

commands.text: aws sqs send-message --queue-url <standard-queue-url-from-task-2> --message-body "Delayed SQS test message" --delay-seconds 10 --region eu-west-2

commands.expectedOutput: The command returns the delayed message after it becomes available, or an empty result if no message becomes available during the wait.

cliSteps.explanation: Uses a 20-second receive wait time to retrieve an available message or return when the wait time expires. Replace the placeholder with the Task 2 queue URL.

tasks.whyItMatters: Queue-level attributes control when messages become available, how long they remain available for processing, how large they can be, and how receive requests behave when no message is immediately available.

tasks.whyItMatters: FIFO queues are used when message order matters or duplicates cannot be tolerated. FIFO queue names must end with .fifo, and sent FIFO messages require a message group ID.

warnings.cost: Amazon SQS requests can incur charges. This Follow Along creates only two small queues and sends only harmless test messages, but delete both queues after verification.
warnings.region: Perform every regional Amazon SQS action in Europe (London), eu-west-2. Queue URLs are Region-specific.
warnings.safety: Use only the fixed queue names and fixed sample messages in this package. Do not send personal, confidential, production, or regulated data. Delete only sqs-basic-test-standard and sqs-basic-test-orders.fifo.

programme.subtitle: sqs-learning-path · Complete beginner replacement for published source revision 3
programme.description: A complete beginner-friendly Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) Follow Along in Europe (London) (eu-west-2). It uses two fixed, harmless queues: sqs-basic-test-standard and sqs-basic-test-orders.fifo.
programme.displayName: Amazon SQS: Basic Message Queue Test
programme.learningOutcome: Use the Amazon SQS console and separate AWS CLI commands to verify access, create standard and FIFO queues, send, receive, delete, delay, and verify harmless test messages, then manually delete only the queues created in this Follow Along.

inputs.buildOutcome: Create and add a complete set of Amazon SQS hands-on labs for the existing Study Tracker app, focused specifically on the AWS Certified Solutions Architect Associate SAA-C03 exam. The app and lab structure already exist, so follow the existing structure, formatting, fields, naming conventions and implementation pattern exactly. Do not describe this as a catalogue, future work, placeholder content, deferred instructions, or something that will be completed later. Every lab must be fully populated and usable. Every lab must be beginner friendly and assume the learner may never have used SQS before. Every lab must contain BOTH complete AWS Management Console steps and complete AWS CLI steps. Never leave Console actions, CLI actions, validation steps, IAM requirements, explanations or cleanup sections empty. Walk the learner through every important click, field, setting and command, explain what each important option does and why it matters, include expected results and verification steps, and keep programming to an absolute minimum. The first lab must create the IAM user and permissions required for the SQS training labs, including creating the user, explaining why root should not be used, assigning suitable permissions using least privilege where practical, signing in as the IAM user, configuring AWS CLI credentials, selecting the region, testing CLI access and verifying SQS permissions. If later labs use Lambda, SNS, S3, CloudWatch, EventBridge, EC2, Auto Scaling or KMS, include the required IAM permissions as part of the relevant lab. Create all practical SQS labs relevant to SAA-C03, including Standard queues; sending, receiving and deleting messages; queue URLs and message IDs; message retention; delay queues; message size; purging and deleting queues; short and long polling; visibility timeout; messages becoming invisible and returning; changing visibility; duplicate processing; at-least-once delivery; best-effort ordering; multiple producers and consumers; FIFO queues; .fifo naming; Message Group IDs; Deduplication IDs; content-based deduplication; ordering; Standard versus FIFO; dead-letter queues; redrive policies; maxReceiveCount; failed and poison messages; moving messages to a DLQ; inspecting and redriving messages; producer to SQS to consumer architectures; worker queues; decoupling; buffering traffic spikes; SQS with Lambda; Lambda retries, failures and batch processing; SNS plus SQS fan-out; S3 event notifications to SQS; EventBridge to SQS; EC2 workers consuming SQS; CloudWatch monitoring and alarms; SQS-driven Auto Scaling; ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible; ApproximateNumberOfMessagesNotVisible; ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage; messages sent, received and deleted; queue policies; SendMessage and ReceiveMessage permissions; service permissions; encryption; KMS and KMS permissions; cross-account SQS; message attributes; large-message patterns using S3; consumer crashes; retry behaviour; permission failures and queue policy failures. Also include practical SAA-C03 comparison and architecture labs covering SQS versus SNS, EventBridge and Kinesis, Standard versus FIFO, SQS versus direct Lambda invocation, traffic spikes, slow backends, failed orders, strict ordering, fan-out, worker failure, serverless processing and Auto Scaling based on queue backlog. Arrange all labs in a logical beginner learning order and implement them directly into the existing app structure as complete labs with no placeholder, deferred, empty or future-content wording.
